Supporting record: claims apply to the revisions and environments named below; this page does not qualify a later candidate.

The exact candidate meets the requirement of no new BiocCheck source-diagnostic categories or instances relative to the actual submitted package. No material regression was found in the bounded semantic, installed-package and pipeline compatibility review. There are no open material findings within this scope.

This conclusion binds source 01bb39ccf8373ae8965a2679ee4813a63ea2d85d and the default-built sceptre_0.99.0.tar.gz with SHA256 606363fce32238354fc0d126d79f515973da7c8287ca43b14ce53ce2d00df4b7. It does not certify Bioconductor acceptance, a release, or untested platforms. The reviewer made no implementation or Git changes.

Actual submission authority and diagnostic comparison

The baseline is submitted source 21f9ea098b69c444a884a49bc254de711968e3b5, independently established from Bioconductor contribution issue 176, the original r-universe run 33438717492, its pinned source tree, source-job inputs and downloaded original artifacts. The original archive SHA256 is 5300b3e3adfbb73a9a2173384ea3ec7e57b8cad8612f3fdc8116d5db5156eaf4; its 97 scoped production/documentation files match the submitted Git source. Later PR qualification and the local submission plan were not substituted for this baseline.

The original official environment used BiocCheck 1.49.30, Bioconductor 3.24, R 4.6.1 and Linux x86_64. Its pinned official wrapper already passed no-check-R-ver=TRUE and no-check-bioc-help=TRUE. The candidate comparison uses that original checker and those historical options; no additional source, coding, formatting or documentation checks were disabled.

Original-checker result or flagged source instances Actual submitted package Exact final candidate New final instances
Errors / warnings / notes 0 / 1 / 3 0 / 1 / 3 0 new categories
Functions longer than 50 lines 49 45 0
Lines longer than 80 characters 145 108 0
cat / print calls outside show 9 9 0

The remaining warning about no direct Bioconductor dependency is inherited. No meaningless dependency was introduced to remove it. The three remaining source-note categories are inherited display calls, long functions and long lines.

This is an instance-level conclusion. Independent scans with the unmodified installed checkers and separate source-lineage review establish that all 45 final long functions map one-to-one to unique already-flagged submitted functions, all 108 complete long-line byte strings occur in the submitted source with unique baseline occurrences consumed once, and all nine display operations are inherited. Long-line comparison preserves indentation and leading/trailing whitespace; only line terminators are excluded. Removed lines do not provide numerical credit for new lines. Anonymous methods were identified by enclosure and behavior rather than line numbers. The moved summary print call retains its original operation.

The older local BiocCheck 1.47.26 reports 48 baseline and 44 final long functions. The one-site difference from 1.49.30 is fully explained: its scanner overwrites a duplicate compute_group name, whereas 1.49.30 preserves both inherited methods. The 52-line method and its 46 coding lines are present in both sources. This is checker-version behavior, not an exemption or newly introduced function.

The four categories added by the pre-cleanup refactor are absent: literal-colon sequence construction, paste directly in conditions, superassignment, and missing runnable exported examples. The fixes use ordinary readable code: seq_len, construction of signal text before signalling, local warning state, explicit migration-object threading, and actual lifecycle examples. Source and parsed-expression review found no new suppression, minification, dynamic source loading or hidden runtime implementation.

All-default checks remain a separate result

The reviewer independently ran both original and final archives with BiocCheck 1.47.26, R 4.6.0 and no disabled flags. Both report 1 error, 1 warning and 5 notes. Neither is a clean all-default run.

Both retain the same support.bioconductor.org HTTP timeout error, unchanged minimum-R-version recommendation and administrative mailing-list subscription note, along with the inherited dependency warning and three source-note categories. Diagnostic-category keys agree; the timeout comparison ignores only its elapsed milliseconds. Complete original diagnostics and invocation records are preserved. These extra checks were omitted by the original official wrapper; the successful 0/1/3 comparison must always be described with that historical-option qualification.

Exact source and independent runtime evidence

The frozen pre-cleanup implementation is 169c16e4ba00c687c1f03fe37e9d79a11d01cd8f; its R/native source is also represented by evidence commit a3433c71fd339932e4c2d366e5413e13ad8299c9. Native source, tests, DESCRIPTION and NAMESPACE are unchanged from that implementation. The final R evidence HEAD is 9a4694450b5d456beedc11f3876ecb1cd84cb05c, with no subsequent change to the candidate’s production/source/documentation/test scope.

The reviewer freshly installed the exact archive on macOS ARM64 / R 4.6.0 and independently performed the following checks:

  • Exact archive/Git comparison: 176 scoped source, native, help and test files match. The separate instance reviewer compared 180 files under its documented broader manifest; the semantic reviewer verified all 46 R files. These are distinct manifest scopes.
  • All 1,958 lines of the canonical parsed-expression delta were read. Twenty-three of 46 R files have identical parsed expressions; the other 23 contain the reviewed helper extractions, signal construction or local renaming. Numerical fitting, association worker/traversal bodies, native implementation and generated-wrapper expressions remain unchanged where applicable.
  • 69 focused differential checks passed over separately frozen baseline/candidate functions using the fresh final namespace and native library. Coverage includes all three saved-object schemas and exact migration payloads/stage identities; RunPlans and result provenance/history; family rejection; manifest/context/runtime helpers; sparse ordering/repeats and control policies; warning order/classes and RNG; serial/fork results, worker errors/causes/calls and interrupts; validity; and public output text.
  • 12 installed collector checks passed, including both original findings: conflicting re-certified coefficients reject atomically, repeated cell vectors are absent, diagnostics/removal conflicts leave the caller unchanged, matching warm fits survive, full identities are restored, stale entries are replaced, and retained proposal attributes remain isolated.
  • All three actual installed API examples executed unchanged: prepare_execution, execute_work_unit and collect_execution. Each runs public import/setup/assignment/QC, prepares and executes two units, collects 418 current result rows, and leaves the original screen uncommitted. The identical installed example-body SHA256 is recorded. An initial reviewer topic-selection harness error was corrected with character.only=TRUE; it was not a package failure, and its initial log is retained separately.

The extraction preserves proposal validation/admission order, complete row/unit coverage, cache insertion order and result/fits commit order. Native draws and full context precede the same keyed analyses; integration and full-family correction remain at collection. Migration uses explicit object returns without losing accumulated stages. Warning capture retains propagation and ordering. Changed implementation fingerprints are expected because they hash function bodies and namespace inventory; scientific/cache identity payloads remain preserved. This does not assert that runtime execution certificates from older package builds are interchangeable.

The semantic subreport states that broad qualification was pending at the time it was written. That snapshot is preserved unchanged. The terminal broad receipts described next were subsequently reviewed and resolve that pending status for this consolidated review.

Owner terminal receipts reviewed separately

The reviewer inspected and copied 13 owner receipt files, verifying their bytes against Git evidence HEAD 9a4694450b5d456beedc11f3876ecb1cd84cb05c. These support:

  • Default package build and vignette build passed.
  • Source suite: 253 cases / 5,641 passing assertions, zero failures, errors, warnings or skips, with 190 source/test hashes unchanged during qualification.
  • Exact installed archive: R CMD check --no-manual --no-build-vignettes reports Status: OK, with 5,641 passing assertions, examples and running vignette code. The separate default build built the vignette; this is not a PDF-manual or check-time vignette-rebuild claim.
  • Seven installed historical-parity workflows produced 231 tolerance-zero comparisons covering tables, preparation/fits, warnings and RNG. Historical reference results were reused, not newly fitted.
  • Both original-matched BiocCheck 1.49.30 and older 1.47.26 runs report 0/1/3 under the original official options; invocation files and complete logs are included.

These broad runs were performed by the implementation owner. The independent reviewer executed the focused checks above and verified the terminal broad evidence; the report does not imply an independent rerun of the entire numerical suite. Older platform and minimum-R receipts retain their older artifact identity.

Isolated pipeline compatibility refresh

The reviewed pipeline production baseline remains 818a156a8a53cf3e34e58b05bd37d115eb4ced49 in /Users/ekatsevi/.codex/worktrees/bioc-compatibility-refresh/sceptre-pipeline. All 23 production/runtime-config/test/container-recipe files are unchanged. Evidence commits are 6d35036ffab74f9e1201199f11824e90beb06044 and bfce9a812c45a7a9e389f1650ff2b42745c7ea89. Their other changes are documentation/evidence and narrow .gitattributes rules preserving original log/session whitespace. The latter commit contains the previously omitted installed-package/session metadata, and all 19 committed evidence-manifest entries and 13 original copied receipts were verified.

The exact new local image is sha256:1510c16a1d5f0da6a266f8685c4b06fa1865e0116b159956af9625dd1cc249b2. Independent network-disabled, no-host-mount container inspection verified the embedded archive bytes and source identity. Runtime is Linux ARM64, R 4.5.1, SCEPTRE 0.99.0, ondisc 1.3.1, Rhdf5lib 1.30.0 and OpenBLAS. The installed SCEPTRE identity is 8f59580aaf43aee9218bb379acda39d7ce1004e8fe65e4a2012a0a7ce98dec9b; scientific reports and Docker signatures agree. Native SCEPTRE and ondisc binary identities were checked directly, including their equality to the previous native binaries.

New-image terminal receipts reviewed: direct and distributed suites each pass nine memory plus two required backed cases without skips; representative distributed high-MOI CRT and reference low-NT empirical-permutation Docker workflows equal same-image direct full tables/plans; distributed resume is 17 cached tasks plus one validation, reference resume seven cached plus one validation; actual injected worker failure prevents collector submission and completed discovery publication. Guard harnesses reject changed nested literal configs, dynamic includes, missing/cyclic configs, legacy flags, output collisions, changed seeds and altered source. The installed public example passes inside the image.

All 72 selected historical/new saved payloads agree across nine cases and eight stages, including standalone power/discovery after QC. This comparison reuses saved historical 169c16e results against newly executed 01bb39c results; the historical source was not rerun.

At final report creation, the pipeline HEAD is still bfce9a8. Its only uncommitted change is the owner’s documentation clarification explicitly qualifying 0/1/3 by the original checker options and distinguishing the all-default diagnostics. That diff and exact documentation snapshot are recorded in pipeline-final-worktree-readback.json; no production/config/test/recipe change is present. A later evidence-only commit may copy this review without altering its frozen qualification identities. The earlier pipeline subreport’s clean-checkout statement describes its own earlier readback.

Limits and handoff

The pipeline scope is local Linux ARM64 with the unchanged literal-local external configuration policy. No new hosted CI, nf-test, external-body marker probe, large-screen, cluster/cloud, Apptainer, AMD64, Windows, minimum-R-floor or cross-platform numerical qualification is claimed. The separate dirty 72cc arrays/HPC feature worktree was neither reviewed nor qualified. Arbitrary stack-trace frame identity is outside the semantic extraction claim. No image publication, merge, release, maintainer outreach or Bioconductor acceptance occurred.

final-verification.json binds the conclusions and supporting reports. final-review-artifact-manifest.json lists exact original paths, sizes and SHA256 hashes for this report and the curated handoff evidence. The earlier baseline-identities.json, BASELINE_AND_FIX_SCOPE.md and baseline manifest are preserved as phase-specific historical evidence; their final-candidate-pending text is superseded by this report, not silently rewritten. Raw private Compass context and copied local submission-plan files are excluded. Live Compass retrieval was limited to the relevant Bioconductor project note; no exhaustive personal-knowledge review is claimed.
